table_reddening.source: Answered from the publishing table rather than inferred from its file name. Clocchiatti et al. 2011, AJ 141, 163, DOI 10.1088/0004-6256/141/5/163, section 3: "Using the computed reddening and K corrections unreddened and transformed to the rest frame the photometry of SN 1998bw given in Table 2.  The results, fitted with low-degree piecewise polinomial and/or spline fits to provide daily sampling, are presented in Table 3."  What was removed is stated too: "it is reasonable to assume a typical Milky Way extinction law to unredden the lights curves presented here. We take as a model the extinction curve of Cardelli, Clayton, & Mathis 1989 with R_V = 3.1", computed "a time dependent extinction in each passbands using the excellent series of spectra of Patat et al. 2001".  Note the shape of that declaration: it is *one* screen fitted to the observed spectra, so it absorbs the Galactic, the host and any circumstellar term together rather than reporting them separately -- which is why both flags are `true` and neither is a per-component measurement.  The paper's own grounds for that choice: "The Galactic dust towards ESO184-G82 contributes A_V ~ 0.2, according to Schlegel, Finkbeiner & Davis 1998", while "Patat et al. 2001 ... did not find Na D absorption lines neither at the redshift of ESO184-G82 nor zero, and set upper limits to the extinction consistent even with the higher estimate".  The practical consequence for a caller: the table is already de-reddened, so adding a `Reddening` here is adding a second term; `predict` detects that state and warns, and `meta["table_reddening"]` echoes what was already removed.  Worth noting how close this came to being read wrong: the paper's Table 3 prints its columns as U0, B0, V0, Rc0, Ic0, while the compiled CSV in data/raw spells the last two Rc and Ic.  The subscript that says "unreddened" was dropped for exactly the two columns whose names then look like ordinary Cousins magnitudes -- which is why the declaration is quoted from the paper here and never inferred from a file name or a column header.

unfold.correction_model: per-epoch, penalised second difference in time
unfold.gain_definition: dM_band / d(log10 L_nu at the node), finite difference on the assembled surface; -2.5 is the delta-band limit

band_admission.rule: one departure at a time, worst excess first, undone when it pushed a band that was inside the cap outside it

template.label: SN 1998bw / GRB 980425 (broad-lined Ic SNe, nearby)
template.z_source: As used by the publishing source of this table: Clocchiatti et al. 2011, AJ 141, 163, DOI 10.1088/0004-6256/141/5/163, section 3 -- "the K-corrections, which, at the redshift of ESO184-G82 (Foley et al. 2006, z = 0.0087,) are expected to be small, but still variable in time".  The same paper's distance (below) is said to be computed from that redshift, so the table's phase axis, its K-corrections and its distance are all on one value; adopting it keeps this manifest internally consistent with the source it came from.  v1 hard-coded 0.0085 with no stated source.  The frame is not stated by either text and is therefore left undeclared rather than guessed: for this template the distance is measured, so z enters only through the (1+z) factors, where 0.0002 in z is 2e-4 mag -- a seventh of one percent of the 0.151 mag the distance error contributes.

distance.source: The kind is `redshift-velocity-field` and not `measured`, which is the whole content of this paragraph.  Read off Clocchiatti et al. 2011, AJ 141, 163, DOI 10.1088/0004-6256/141/5/163, which is the publishing source of this table (see `provenance`): "The distance to ESO 184-G082 was taken to be 37.3 +- 2.6 Mpc, as computed by the NED database from the redshift measured by Foley et al. 2006, a Hubble constant of 74.2 km/s/Mpc (Riess et al. 2009), and the model of the local velocity field given by Mould et al. 2000."  So this is a redshift-derived distance with a velocity-field correction, quoted with its error -- which is what makes the distance term of the error budget real rather than zero (2.6/37.3 = 7.0 % in fractional distance, i.e. 0.151 mag of distance modulus).  That 7 % is independently confirmed inside the same paper: both flux columns of its Table 3 carry the footnote "Uncertainty does not include the ~7 % uncertainty in the distance", which is the same 2.6/37.3 and the reason a distance error has to travel with the distance.  The host is the one this paper names, ESO 184-G82; the two catalogue strings v1 carried for it (ES024014.1-251413, E186-G210) were not reconciled against a catalogue in this build, so they are not repeated here.

citations:
table + distance + reddening: Clocchiatti et al. 2011, AJ 141, 163, "The ultimate
       light curve of SN 1998bw/GRB 980425", DOI 10.1088/0004-6256/141/5/163.  This is the
       publishing source of data/raw/SN980425_intrinsic_lc.csv: its Table 3 is that file
       (same 16 columns, same values row for row), and every block above is quoted from
       it.  Read via arXiv:1106.1695.

K-correction formalism: Hogg, Baldry, Blanton & Eisenstein 2002, "The K
       correction", arXiv:astro-ph/0210394.  Never refereed, so it has no journal ref
       and no DOI: cite the arXiv id. Equations used: 2 (m_R = M_Q + DM + K_QR),
       3 (DM = 5 log10(D_L/10 pc)), 6 (L_nu = 4 pi D_L^2 f_nu / (1+z))

Photon-counting SN K-correction: Nugent, Kim & Perlmutter 2002, PASP 114, 803,
       DOI 10.1086/341707.  Cited for the method, not by equation: its equations
       were not read off a proof here
